title: Telemetry escrow: weighted path resolver combining p50/p95 and network health
creator: Priya Nair
description: Implement a region/tier path resolver that fuses p50 and p95 latency telemetry with a compact network health score, and protects decisions with an "escrow" (grace + cooldown) mechanism to prevent oscillation. The resolver should produce a ranked list of candidate POPs and associated fallback model variants per tier, respect release/priority overrides, and expose signals for the Console and runtime tracing hooks.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Nair: Initial RFC posted to Confluence outlining escrow concept, formula for compositeScore = w1*normalized_p50 + w2*normalized_p95 + w3*netHealthPenalty + tierPenalty; proposed default weights (0.4, 0.4, 0.15, 0.05). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/Telemetry-Escrow-Weighted-Path-Resolver

2026-03-03 Mateo Ruiz: Prototype implemented in the simulator (runtime/region_resolver/sim) that computes compositeScore per POP. Basic hysteresis: require compositeScore improvement > 7% and persist for 30s before switching; cooldown 180s. Observed flip-flop reduction in sim trace set A (50 simulated candidate bursts). Perf note: scoring adds ~120ns/op in hot path; batching mitigates overhead.

2026-03-05 Arielle Chen (SRE): Reviewed failure modes. Suggested adding a 'path escrow' that retains last-usable POP for retries on intermittent packet loss spikes; recommended coalescing telemetry windows for link drops vs latency spikes. Logged concerns about telemetry skew during cross-pop deployment rollouts.

2026-03-06 Design feedback (Oliver Zhang): Console UX should surface the escrow timeline and show when a POP is 'soft-evicted' vs 'hard-failed'. Mockup added to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEF_design_mockups

2026-03-08 Mateo Ruiz: PR created implementing resolver core and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1198. Integration tests added that exercise p50/p95 divergence, netHealth degradations, and variant fallback ordering. Testbench results attached to PR.

2026-03-09 QA (Sasha Park): Ran localized canary using playground workload. Observed expected behavior: when p95 jumps without p50 shift, compositeScore penalizes candidate but does not immediately evict thanks to escrow; requests routed to fallback variant for 2% of traffic during stabilization window. Logged one regression: TTL on cached composite scores was too long (5m) causing slow recovery; reduced to 45s.

2026-03-11 Security review (Anika Rao): No secrets handled by resolver. Recommend opt-in flag for private deployments where telemetry sources may be restricted. Marked security_review_required=false for hosted default behavior.

2026-03-12 Mateo Ruiz: Engineering rollout plan approved. Staged canary: 0->5->20->50% over 4 hours with automatic rollback if user-facing error rate increases >0.5% or avg tail latency delta > 15% at p95. Dashboard panels: latency composite, escrow state transitions, chosen variant distribution. Dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/route/escrow-resolver-canary
notes: Trade-offs: higher weight on p95 improves tail protection but can reduce throughput if variant fallbacks are conservative. Escrow window and cooldown are tunables; we will expose them as policy config per customer/tier. Follow-on work: A/B experiment to optimize weights per workload and automatic weight tuning based on historical SLAs. Monitoring hooks include trace tags: resolver.v=2, escrow.state, chosen.variant.
